pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do when you use a simile or metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   B. Never explain it
   C. Use hurtful comparisons
   D. Use very many in one sentence

2. Why should you not translate a saying from your language word for word? (1 mark)
   A. Words are never important
   B. The meaning may be lost
   C. It is against the law
   D. It is always easy

3. How can you find the meaning of a new word in a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Tear the page
   B. Ignore it always
   C. Ask no one
   D. Use the context and check a dictionary

4. What is a level reader? (1 mark)
   A. A type of dictionary
   B. A tool for measuring floors
   C. A book written for a particular reading level
   D. A machine

5. Why do many readers read silently? (1 mark)
   A. It is illegal to read aloud
   B. It is fast and does not disturb others
   C. Books cannot be read aloud
   D. It is boring

6. Why should you plan before writing a story? (1 mark)
   A. To avoid a title
   B. To finish early
   C. To organise your ideas
   D. To make it longer

7. What is a portfolio of proverbs? (1 mark)
   A. A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   B. A kind of bag for money
   C. A poem
   D. A game

8. Which question helps you plan an experience to tell? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the moon?
   B. What colour is the wall?
   C. Who was there?
   D. How long is the ruler?

9. Which sentence joins two events with when? (1 mark)
   A. I smiled the gift.
   B. Saw I gift.
   C. When the gift.
   D. I smiled when I saw the gift.

10. Which of these should you include when describing an event? (1 mark)
   A. Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   B. Only the name
   C. Nothing
   D. Only the date

11. Where can the main idea often be found? (1 mark)
   A. In the first sentence of a paragraph
   B. Only in the last word
   C. In the page number
   D. Nowhere

12. Which strategy would you use to see what a newspaper article is about? (1 mark)
   A. Painting
   B. Cutting
   C. Skimming
   D. Scanning for a number

13. What is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A list
   B. Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   C. A title
   D. A sentence with one word

14. What does a simple sentence have? (1 mark)
   A. One subject and one predicate
   B. No verb
   C. Two subjects always
   D. No capital

15. What does a preposition show? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of a thing
   B. The price of goods
   C. The position of one thing in relation to another
   D. The sound of an animal

16. Who should you call for a sick animal? (1 mark)
   A. A shopkeeper
   B. A veterinary doctor
   C. A tailor
   D. A driver

17. In choral recitation, the group (1 mark)
   A. writes the poem
   B. sings only
   C. reads silently
   D. says the poem together at the same pace

18. What does intonation add to a poem? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A new title
   C. Extra pages
   D. The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling

19. Which question helps you find ideas from a picture? (1 mark)
   A. What page is this?
   B. Who printed it?
   C. How heavy is the paper?
   D. Who is in the picture?

20. How should peer feedback be given? (1 mark)
   A. Loudly
   B. Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   C. Never
   D. Rudely

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain what a subject and a predicate are, then write one sentence and divide it. (5 marks)

22. Mama Neema buys a box of bananas for 200 shillings and sells it for 260 shillings. Find her profit. (2 marks)

23. Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor and give an example of each. (4 marks)

24. Write one simile and one metaphor about a teacher. (3 marks)

25. List three tips for reciting a poem well. (3 marks)

26. Explain what a story setting is. (2 marks)

27. Join the sentences with when: I counted my money. The bell rang. (2 marks)

28. A picture shows a girl beside a thin dog under a tree with an empty bowl. Write a story plan and a four-sentence story. (5 marks)

29. Describe how to mark a line of a poem for reading aloud. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   Clear and kind comparisons work best.

2. B — The meaning may be lost
   Sayings often carry meaning beyond the words.

3. D — Use the context and check a dictionary
   Context clues and a dictionary help.

4. C — A book written for a particular reading level
   Level readers match the skills of the pupils.

5. B — It is fast and does not disturb others
   Silent reading is quiet and lets you think.

6. C — To organise your ideas
   A plan gives your story a clear shape.

7. A — A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   A portfolio holds the class collection.

8. C — Who was there?
   Who, what, where, when, why and how help plan a story.

9. D — I smiled when I saw the gift.
   It uses when to link two events.

10. A — Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   These details make the event clear.

11. A — In the first sentence of a paragraph
   First sentences often give the main idea.

12. C — Skimming
   You want the main idea.

13. B — Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   It joins two ideas.

14. A — One subject and one predicate
   Simple sentences have one main idea.

15. C — The position of one thing in relation to another
   Prepositions show position such as on, under and beside.

16. B — A veterinary doctor
   Veterinary doctors treat animals.

17. D — says the poem together at the same pace
   Choral means together.

18. D — The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   Intonation shows meaning.

19. D — Who is in the picture?
   Who, where, what and why give story ideas.

20. B — Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   Kind feedback helps writers.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: The subject is who or what the sentence is about and the predicate says what the subject does. Example: The girl (subject) counts the coins (predicate).
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two meanings, one for a sentence, and two marks for the correct division.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: 260 minus 200 equals 60 shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the working and one mark for the answer with units.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: A simile compares using like or as, for example as quick as lightning. A metaphor says one thing is another, for example Time is money.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition and one for each example.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Simile: The teacher is as patient as a rock. Metaphor: The teacher is a walking dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a simile, one for a metaphor, one for clearly showing the difference.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Learn it well, mark pauses and stressed words, speak clearly, look at the audience, keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: The setting is the place and time where the story happens.
   Working / marking points: One mark for place and one for time.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: When I counted my money, the bell rang.
   Working / marking points: One mark for using when and one mark for the comma.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan with title, characters, setting, problem and ending, followed by four sentences that show the girl helping the dog and end with a lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, setting and problem, and two marks for a clear four-sentence story.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Underline words to stress, draw a slash where you will pause, read the line using your marks and check that it sounds natural.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.
